title: Coleoptera 64-species x 16-locus design (PREPRINT-18 dimensions) vs. published phylogenomics
purpose: Repeat the seqnet -> RuNIE validation at the dataset size of PREPRINT-18 (coleoptera-ecosystem-function-preprint): 64 species and 16 loci, mitochondrial loci taken from complete mitogenomes. PREPRINT-18 only sets the dimensions and taxon design; it is not a validation source. Final trees are scored against clades reported in the published studies below. A clade is testable when the run samples >= 2 tips inside and >= 2 outside it, and recovered when the unrooted tree contains the corresponding bipartition.

design_reference.taxon_design: 10 species each of Carabidae, Scarabaeidae, Coccinellidae, Cerambycidae, Chrysomelidae and Curculionidae; 1 Cupedidae (Archostemata); 1 Hydroscaphidae (Myxophaga); 2 Neuropterida outgroups (Nemopteridae; antlion lineage)
design_reference.locus_interpretation: PREPRINT-18 reports a 16-locus supermatrix but lists 13 mitochondrial protein-coding genes + 12S + 16S + six nuclear loci (21 named). Its five functional nuclear gene families (GH45, GH28, GH5, aquaporin, CYP6) were multi-copy paralog families sampled from a few species (mostly predicted mRNAs), so they are not species-level orthologous markers. This design uses the 15 mitogenome loci + nuclear 28S = 16 loci.
design_reference.outgroup_note: NCBI Taxonomy has no Ascalaphidae (owlflies sit inside Myrmeleontidae), so the antlion-lineage outgroup is sampled from Myrmeleontidae.

sources.citation: McKenna, D. D., et al. (2019). The evolution and genomic basis of beetle diversity. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 116(49), 24729-24737.
Zhang, S.-Q., Che, L.-H., Li, Y., Pang, H., Slipinski, A., & Zhang, P. (2018). Evolutionary history of Coleoptera revealed by extensive sampling of genes and species. Nature Communications, 9, 205.
